prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

The profile below describes the moral priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  care: 0.30
  equality: 0.20
  authority: 0.19
  loyalty: 0.16
  proportionality: 0.10
  sanctity: 0.05
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
Scope
- Applies mainly to England due to devolution. Scottish and Welsh proposals may differ.

Fiscal approach and tax
- Reprioritise about £5bn annually by abolishing certain subsidies and departments/functions, cancelling ID cards, and diverting Child Trust Fund money to education.
- Introduce a 50% income tax rate only on earnings above £100,000 to fund: abolition of university tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly/disabled people; and cutting local taxes by replacing Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay.
- Independent scrutiny of budgets by the National Audit Office; greater ONS independence.
- Typical household local tax bill reduced by about £450 under Local Income Tax.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis via expanded access to scans/tests, weekend/evening operation, and staffing/training.
- Free eye and dental checks; broaden prescription charge exemptions for long‑term conditions.
- More clinicians; scrap central targets; more local accountability.
- NHS dentistry contract reform and personal dental plans.
- Health MOTs, personal care plans for long‑term conditions, stronger mental health rights, end age discrimination.
- Public health: school nutrition standards, limit junk‑food ads to children, ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition/top‑up fees; restore grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund budget to hire 21,000 teachers; infant classes average 20, junior 25; extended school hours; 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Subject-specialist teaching in core subjects; reduce high‑stakes testing at 7 and 11; stronger SEN support; behaviour plans and managed transfers.
- Unified academic/vocational diplomas from 14; fund parity for colleges; maintain statutory school transport distances.
- Green building standards for education estates; strengthen outdoor learning.

Crime, justice, borders and equality
- 10,000 more police (funded by scrapping ID cards) plus complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy, modernise tech.
- Prioritise serious drug crime; expand tough community sentences; anti‑social behaviour tools with underlying support.
- Prisons focused on work, literacy and skills; progress tied to effort.
- Create a UK Border Force; protect jury trial; tighten judicial control of any control orders; allow intercept evidence; repeal flawed terror provisions.
- Overhaul asylum processing via a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; pursue EU common standards.
- Single Equality Act; hate‑crime units in every force.

Economy and business
- Stamp Duty threshold to £150,000.
- Simpler, lighter regulation with impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspections.
- Small‑business rate relief and site‑value rating; fair‑trading duty; English Tourism Board.
- Carbon Tax replacing the Climate Change Levy; incentives for cleaner vehicles and energy‑efficient homes.
- At least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no replacement of aging nuclear plants.

Pensions, benefits and family support
- From 75: basic state pension to at least £109.45 (single) and £167.05 (couple), linked to earnings; residency‑based “citizen’s pension.”
- Replace Council Tax to benefit most pensioners; six months’ maternity pay at minimum‑wage rate.
- Tailored employment support replacing one‑size‑fits‑all schemes; end harsh sanctions on genuine claimants.
- Replace the Child Support Agency with HMRC‑based assessment/enforcement plus specialist tribunal.
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment extended to severely disabled working‑age people; option to invest a year’s payment in insulation.
- Strengthen protection for failed occupational pensions; consult and honour accrued public‑sector pension rights.
- Reduce fraud/error through simplification and prevention.

Housing, local services and environment
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; encourage brownfield reuse via VAT reform; require permission for second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; increase core arts funding with inflation; support grassroots sport.
- Devolve more powers; streamline inspectorates; protect post offices and universal postal service.
- Zero‑waste goal; 60% household recycling within seven years; producer responsibility; climate‑aware planning/building rules.

Transport
- Rail reform with fewer, longer franchises; shift road funds to station safety and key upgrades.
- Reform Vehicle Excise Duty to zero for least‑polluting cars; expand congestion charging tied to upfront public transport investment; long‑term national road pricing to replace fuel duty and VED.
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners/disabled; free railcards for pensioners, disabled people, families and youth.
- Limit major new roads; grow rail freight; develop ports/waterways; aviation: per‑aircraft charging, emissions trading, oppose new SE expansions.

Rural, agriculture and fisheries
- Fair‑trading duty and Food Trade Inspector to protect farm gate prices.
- Accelerate CAP reform toward public goods; support family farms and new entrants.
- Marine Act with conservation zones and regional co‑management; stronger wildlife protection.
- Animal Protection Commission and comprehensive Animal Welfare Act.
- Precaution on GM crops, support GM‑free zones, rigorous labelling; promote organic.

Europe, international affairs and defence
- Support EU institutional reform subject to referendum; prepare for euro entry if conditions met.
- Iraq: back democratic transition, build Iraqi capacity, and aim to withdraw forces with UN mandate expiry.
- Multilateral security, UN and EU reform, human rights focus.
- Defence: address overstretch; improve procurement; reprioritise programmes; maintain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms‑export oversight; back an international arms trade treaty.
- International development: increase aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end agricultural dumping; fair trade access; responsible investment; green development priorities; stronger action on global environmental crime; lead on climate targets (Kyoto plus “contraction and convergence”).

Constitution and governance
- War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; reduce departments/ministers; decentralise to local/regional bodies; fair funding across the UK.
- Extend STV to local and national elections; predominantly elected second chamber; voting age aligned with other civic responsibilities; reform BBC governance via an independent regulator.
- Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement; merge key portfolios into a single environment/transport/energy department.

TEXT_F:
Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

Economy, tax, and regulation
- Save £12bn a year by 2007–08 via a civil service recruitment freeze, removal of 235,000 bureaucratic posts, and cutting/abolishing 168 public bodies.
- Use £8bn of savings to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts in the first Budget; grow total public spending at 4% a year to 2011–12.
- Maintain the minimum wage; halve council tax bills for many pensioner households (up to £500, funded centrally).
- Link the basic state pension to earnings; retain Winter Fuel Payment, free TV licences (75+), and the one-off £200 council tax payment (that year).
- Create Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; encourage “opt-out” workplace pensions; use unclaimed financial assets to help those hit by failed schemes.
- Reduce business regulation via departmental regulatory budgets, sunset reviews, and ending “gold-plating” of EU rules.
- Keep Bank of England independence; retain the pound (no Euro).

Family policy and education
- Flexible maternity pay (over 6 or 9 months); up to £50/week childcare support per under‑5 for eligible working families, with simpler access and choice of formal/informal care; more workplace nurseries and after-school clubs.
- Restore school discipline: heads/governors control admissions and expulsions; create Turnaround Schools; cut teacher paperwork.
- Simplify school funding so money follows the pupil; allow growth of good schools; 600,000 additional places in first term.
- Publish exam marks with grades; allow international qualifications; slim the National Curriculum and increase academic rigour.
- 300,000 vocational grants (£1,000 each) for 14–16-year-olds; two hours of after‑school sport; ban junk food in schools; safer school trips.
- Permit free places at independent schools where costs match state funding.
- Moratorium on closing special schools; reform further education funding and governance; scrap university tuition fees and the admissions regulator; support university endowments.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn a year over the Parliament (to ~£2,000 per head); cut central bureaucracy (abolish Strategic Health Authorities, reduce PCTs/quangos); scrap central targets.
- Greater local autonomy: empower professionals; bring back matrons with ward-closure powers; invest in infection control and single rooms.
- Patient/GP choice of providers; funding follows the patient; protect viable community hospitals.
- Partial NHS rebate (about half NHS cost) for self-funded operations to help reduce waiting lists.
- Social care partnership to avoid forced home sales; more respite/support for carers.
- Improve NHS dentistry access with new contracts and low monthly prepayment schemes.
- Health checks for non‑EU migrants staying over 12 months and for permanent settlement; STI public health campaign.

Crime, justice, and security
- Recruit 5,000 additional police officers per year; cut paperwork; introduce elected police commissioners; focus on neighbourhood policing.
- End early release; add 20,000 prison places; “honesty in sentencing.”
- Expand drug treatment, including 25,000 residential rehab places; reverse cannabis reclassification.
- Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; strengthen counter‑terror capabilities.

Immigration and borders
- 24/7 port surveillance; restore embarkation controls; create a Border Control Police.
- Australian‑style points system for work permits.
- Set an annual overall migration limit, including a quota for UNHCR‑referred refugees; process asylum claims outside the UK; seek national control over asylum rules including changes to international/EU frameworks.

Governance and devolution
- Publish a delivery timetable; strengthen parliamentary scrutiny; reduce MPs by 20%; pursue a largely elected upper chamber.
- Abolish regional assemblies; return planning, housing, transport, and fire service powers to local authorities.
- “English votes for English laws”; Wales referendum on Assembly powers; uphold the consent principle in Northern Ireland.

Communities, transport, environment, and rural
- More local say on planning; stronger action on illegal traveller encampments; devolve arts/lottery funding.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Modernise roads; review all speed cameras; lengthen rail franchises.
- Protect Green Belt; prioritise brownfield development.
- Phase out HFCs; incentivise home energy efficiency; lower VED and grants for low‑emission cars; increase recycling; support renewables and efficiency for energy security.
- Honest food labelling; require Little Red Tractor in public procurement; further CAP reform; strengthen animal welfare; free vote on hunting ban.

Defence and foreign policy
- Increase front‑line defence by £2.7bn by 2007–08; support service families; preserve regiments; retain warships; keep NATO central.
- Support Iraq reconstruction and a Middle East peace based on Israeli security and a viable Palestinian state.
- EU: referendum on the Constitutional Treaty within six months; oppose Euro; seek reform of social/employment rules; repatriate fisheries control; support enlargement (including Turkey).
- Overseas aid: work toward 0.7% of national income by 2013; seek greater national control over aid spending.

Immediate actions (first month/day)
- Begin recruiting extra police; reinstate matrons; first Budget to cut waste and reduce taxes; empower head teachers to expel; initiate 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU referendum date.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_F aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
